name: Sicilian Defense, Wing Gambit
summary: The Sicilian Wing Gambit sacrifices the b-pawn with 2.b4 to deflect Black's c5-pawn and build a broad centre with d4.
intro: The Wing Gambit answers 1.e4 c5 with the immediate 2.b4, offering the b-pawn so that after 2...cxb4 3.a3 White can deflect Black's c-pawn, seize the centre with d4 and open the a- and b-files for rapid, attacking play.

sections.heading: Strategic ideas
paragraphs: White's idea is straightforwardly aggressive: by luring the c5-pawn to b4 and then playing a3, White removes Black's main lever against the centre and prepares to erect an ideal d4/e4 pawn duo. In return for the pawn White gains time, open files and easy development.

Black's task is to prove that the extra pawn outweighs White's initiative. Accurate defenders return the pawn at the right moment, strike in the centre with ...d5, and complete development smoothly, after which the healthier structure often favours Black.

sections.heading: Main variations
paragraphs: After 3.a3 Black can accept with 3...bxa3, opening lines but handing White quick development, or decline and consolidate. A common and reliable equaliser is the central counter ...d5, meeting White's ambitions head-on before the big centre can be completed.

White typically follows with d4, Nf3 and Bc4 or Bd3, aiming pieces at f7 while the open a- and b-files feed the rooks. If Black is careless the initiative can snowball; with precise play Black neutralises the pressure and keeps the material.

sections.heading: History and background
paragraphs: Wing gambits against the Sicilian are old, romantic-era ideas that trade material for speed. Today the line is regarded as offbeat and objectively harmless against best play, yet it remains a popular surprise weapon in rapid and club chess, where its open, tactical character can catch an unprepared opponent.
